This Review Petition Is Filed Under Order Xlvii Rule
1 Read With Section 114 Of Cpc Praying To Review The
Judgment And Order Dated 07.04.2010 In
M.F.A.No.2497/2005 And Set Aside/Modify The Impugned
Judgment Absolving The Liability Fixed On The Petitioner
Insurance Company To Pay The Enhanced Compensation
To Respondent Nos.1 And 2 Herein In The Interest Of
Justice And Equity.
 This Review Petition Coming On For Final Hearing,
This Day, K.S.Mudagal.J, Made The Following:
 Order
Heard.
2.  In this matter, Sri Shripad V.Shastri, learned Counsel has filed vakalat only for respondent No.2.
Respondent No.3 was served and unrepresented in M.F.A.No.2497/2005 regarding which this review petition is filed.
Therefore notice to him is dispensed with.
3. This petition is filed seeking review of the judgment of this Court dated 07.04.2010 in M.F.A.No.2497/2005.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 filed M.V.C.No.4997/2002 before XIV Additional MACT and Small Causes Court, Bangalore claiming compensation for death of their son Seby Cyriac.

entities.text: XIV Additional MACT and Small Causes Court, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In that case, the Tribunal by award NC: 2023:KHC:21333-DB dated 12.11.2003 had awarded compensation of Rs.7,81,500/-.
4.
The review petitioner challenged that order before this Court in M.F.A.No.8520/2004.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 contested the said appeal before this Court.

This Court on hearing both the parties by judgment dated 15.03.2010 partly allowed the appeal of the petitioner and reduced the compensation from Rs.7,81,500/- to Rs.5,43,200/-.
5.
In the meantime, respondent Nos.1 and 2 also had filed M.F.A.No.2497/2005 seeking enhancement of the compensation.

In both the cases, Insurer was represented by different Counsel,
but the claimants were represented by the same Counsel.
M.F.A.No.2497/2005 was disposed on 07.04.2010 enhancing the compensation by Rs.40,000/- in addition to Rs.7,81,500/-.

sentences.text:
The records show that when M.F.A.No.2497/2005 came up for hearing, none of the parties brought to the notice of the Court about filing of M.F.A.No.8520/2004 of the Insurer and disposal of the same on 15.03.2010.
7.
To execute the award in M.F.A.No.2497/2005, respondent Nos.1 and 2 filed Execution Case No.884/2020 NC: 2023:KHC:21333-DB before the Tribunal.

The petitioner claims that the fact of the claimants securing subsequent order in M.F.A.No.2497/2005 in suppression of the earlier order in MFA No.8520/2004 was surfaced only when it received the attachment warrant in Execution case No.884/2020.

8. Petitioner's Counsel submits that respondent Nos.1 and 2 have played fraud by suppressing the judgment in M.F.A.No.8520/2004 and in view of earlier judgment in MFA No.8520/2004 subsequent judgment in MFA No.2497/2005 needs to be reviewed.
9. Sri Shripad V.Shastri, learned Counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2 submits that since during 2010 there was no digitalization, he failed to note that two cases were filed against the same award.
He further submits that when M.F.A.No.2497/2005 came up for hearing, he had forgotten disposal of earlier appeal i.e. M.F.A.No.8520/2004.
He seeks to justify the action of respondent Nos.1 and 2 on the ground that even the petitioner is also equally negligent.
He submits that in the petitioner's office they maintain the records and they should have been vigilant of two cases when they too appeared and were heard in both cases.
Admittedly, in both the appeals, the petitioner was represented by different Counsel.
Further any negligence on the part of the Officials in the petitioner's office does not give any handle to respondent Nos.1 and 2 to make unlawful gain by abusing the process of Court.
They were represented in both cases by common Counsel.
They were even aware that petitioner was represented by different advocate in both the cases.
11. To crown all these they have filed Execution Petition No.884/2020 and proceeded to seek attachment of the movable properties of the petitioner.

By that time, they had already received compensation awarded by the Tribunal which was reduced by this Court in M.F.A.No.8520/2004.
12.
If at all there was any dereliction of duty on the part of the officials, at the most they may give cause to the petitioner to initiate disciplinary proceedings against such officials.
But that does not mitigate misconduct of respondent Nos.1 and 2 i.e. the claimants.
By such of their acts, respondent Nos.1 and 2 have not only abused the process of Court, they have even played fraud on the Court.
Though learned Counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2 contended that on learning about such mistake, he filed an application in M.F.A.No.8520/2004 to recall that order.
Firstly no material is placed in support of the same.

Secondly, if at all any such application was to be filed that should The New India Assurance Co., Ltd vs Sri Cyriac K C on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126723079/
3 have been filed in the subsequent case i.e. M.F.A.No.2497/2005.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co., Ltd vs Sri Cyriac K C
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That also shows that respondent Nos.1 and 2 had inclination to adopt unethical practice only to make wrongful gain.
14. It is no doubt true that Sri Shripad V Shastri, learned Counsel conceded for recalling the order but that does not relieve the persons responsible for such misconduct.
Sri Shripad V Shastri, learned Counsel reported that claimant No.1 died.
The original death certificate is not produced.
Even if the same is accepted, respondent No.1 is survived by respondent No.2.
Therefore this petition does not abate.
15. Order XLVII Rule 1 of CPC provides for review of the order, if it is found that such order suffers apparent error on the face of the record or for any sufficient reasons.

As the judgment in MFA No.8520/2004 had attained finality the second judgment in MFA No.2497/2005 between the same NC: 2023:KHC:21333-DB parties on the same issues is an error apparent on the face of the record.
16. Apart from that fraud played by respondent Nos.1 and 2 and their counsel is sufficient reason to recall the order.

Such acts of respondent Nos.1 and 2 is nothing but the act of obstructing the administration of justice which is criminal contempt within the meaning of Section 2(c) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.
For the aforesaid reasons, this review petition deserves to be allowed with costs and recommending for necessary action against the concerned respondents and other concerned involved in the case.
Hence the following:
ORDER The review petition is allowed.
The judgment and the order dated 07.04.2010 in M.F.A.No.2497/2005 is hereby recalled.

The appeal in M.F.A.No.2497/2005 is dismissed with costs of Rs.1,00,000/- payable by respondent Nos.1 and 2 to the Karnataka Legal Services Authority within four w e e k s f r o m t h e d a t e o f t h i s o r d e r f a i l i n g w h i c h t h e M e m b e r N C :
2023:KHC:21333-DB Secretary of Karnataka Legal Services Authority shall recover the same in execution of this order.
Further Registrar (Judicial) is requested to place the matter before Hon'ble the Chief Justice for initiation of contempt of Court proceedings against the claimants and other concerned in the case.

Sd/-
JUDGE Sd/-
JUDGE KSR
